error.signature: AI tells a foreigner in Malaysia that public/government hospital treatment costs the same as for Malaysian citizens, or is free / heavily subsidised the way it is for citizens

verdict.summary: Under the Fees Act 1951 as amended by the Fees (Medical)(Cost of Services) Order 2014 (fully enforced from January 2016), non-citizens are billed on a separate, far higher fee schedule at Malaysian government hospitals and clinics than the heavily subsidised citizen rate - e.g. roughly RM40 vs RM1 for outpatient registration and RM100 vs RM3 for a specialist clinic visit, with much larger gaps for deliveries, radiotherapy, and inpatient ward stays.

dead_ends.action: Assume a foreigner or expat will be charged the same subsidised citizen rate (e.g. roughly RM1 outpatient registration) at a Malaysian government hospital or clinic
dead_ends.why_fails: The Fees (Medical)(Cost of Services) Order 2014, made under the Fees Act 1951 and fully enforced from January 2016, put non-citizens on a separate fee schedule - roughly RM40 vs RM1 for outpatient registration and RM100 vs RM3 for a specialist clinic visit, because the public healthcare subsidy is built around citizens, not visitors or foreign workers.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Government hospitals are usually associated with subsidised or near-free care, so people assume the subsidy applies uniformly to anyone treated there rather than being billed by citizenship status.

dead_ends.action: Tell an undocumented migrant or asylum seeker they will be charged the identical full 'foreigner' rate with no discount at a government facility
dead_ends.why_fails: UNHCR-registered refugees and asylum-seekers are billed at 50% of the standard foreigner fee under an arrangement with the Ministry of Health, so treating every non-citizen as paying the full foreigner rate overstates the cost for that specific registered group (unregistered/undocumented individuals do pay the full foreigner fee).

workarounds.action: Budget for non-citizen fee tiers before visiting a Malaysian government hospital or clinic - outpatient visits and especially inpatient/ward stays, deliveries, and radiotherapy run many times the citizen price, and expect to settle the bill before or shortly after discharge.

If you or a family member are a UNHCR-registered refugee or asylum-seeker, present your UNHCR documentation at registration to be billed at the reduced 50%-of-foreigner rate instead of the full non-citizen rate.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers non-resident bank account payment limits; this one covers a completely separate non-citizen fee schedule at government hospitals.
